To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the neutron-rich nuclei 34,35Mg and the proton-rich nucleus 33Na have been studied in-beam gamma-ray experiments, which have revealed new excited states.
we observed the first gamma-ray transitions in the neutron-rich odd-mass nucleus 35Mg.

the first gamma-ray transitions have been observed in 35M Mg, which completes the level scheme up to spin-parity 5+ and 3+ for the odd-odd 35Mg nucleus, and that the first gamma rays have been observed from the 7/2 + 1 state in 33Na.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of very neutron-rich nuclei, which is a key to understanding the evolution of the nuclear shell structure towards the neutron dripline.
the spectroscopy of neutron-rich isotopes close to the proton drip-line, where the shell-model description is challenged by the presence of intruder configurations.
the structure of nuclei far from the valley of stability and is aimed at a better understanding of the shell evolution and the interplay of single-particle and collective degrees of freedom.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both 33Na and 35Mg are part of the "island of inversion" at N = 20.

the 35Mg nucleus, which is an odd-N nucleus and thus not part of the "N = 20 Island of Inversion", is not as well described in the framework of a shell-model calculation as the neighboring 36Mg and 34Mg nuclei.

the present results provide a new benchmark for shell-model calculations and that the experimental data are in good overall agreement with the theoretical predictions, which is a very encouraging result for the applicability of shell-model calculations for the description of nuclei in this region of the nuclear chart.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the neutron 1p-1h intruder states in 33Na are found to be very similar to those observed in 33Al.

we have been able to identify and characterize the first excited states in two very neutron-rich N = 21 and N = 19 isotones, 35Mg(3/2+) and 33Na(7/2+), respectively, and that the observed states in 35Mgsatisfy the expectations of the shell-model.
we have observed the first excited 0+ state in 33Na, the first gamma-ray decay of an intruder state in 35Mga and the first gamma-ray transitions in the odd-Z nucleus 33Na.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the neutron-rich nuclei around N = 21 and Z = 11 are very promising for future experiments that aim for a more detailed understanding of the structure of the very neutron-rich Mg and Na isotopes.
the neutron 2p2h intruder configurations play a crucial role for the description of the low-energy structure in the neutron-rich Mg and Na isotopes.
the neutron 1p-1h intruder states are not strongly populated in the fragmentation reactions, which allows us to probe the neutron 2p2h intruder configurations in the neutron-rich nuclei.
